newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- ends higher as supply dries up. [CORRECTED 06:40 GMT 10/5]
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- ends higher as supply dries up. [CORRECTED 06:40 GMT 10/5]

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices recovered small gains lost momentarily at midday to finish Friday's session 1/8 to 1/4 higher.
The better tone came ahead of one of the lowest supply week's of the year, with next week's total only barely crossing the $1 billion mark.
Traders said Friday's late-day gains followed the same move in Treasuries, where the long bond was up 1/2 at 94-16/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
"There was a blip at the end," one muni analyst said. But he added that activity levels in the afternoon were extremely light so some of the gains were on quotes, not actual trades.
The analyst said high-grade bonds improved about two basis points, and slightly more on the long-end.
Much of the moves during the day came as participants evaluated and then reevaluated statements Thursday night from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.

The early concensus was that Greenspan was suggesting another interest rate increase might not be necessary, helping to boost prices. But some investors then took a second look at Greenspan's remarks and decided that conclusion was not assured.

Debt futures also regained ground lost earlier in the day. June municipal bonds finished 16/32 higher at 115-25/32, while June Treasury bonds gained 13/32 to 110-7/32. The MOB spread between the two contracts widened to 178 ticks from 175 at the close on Thursday.

In the secondary market, Chicago Board of Education AMBAC 5-3/4s of 2020 were bid at 5.88 percent, down one basis point. Port of Seattle FGIC 5-1/2s of 2022 were bid at 5.79 percent, also one basis point lower.

Municipal bond sales for next week are expected to total $2.2 billion (Corrects from $1.1 billion) in 110 sales, the lowest total since late March, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Negotiated offerings total $1.3 billion (Corrects from $128 million) in 34 sales, with a three-part $400 million Municipal Assistance Corp for the City of New York deal through Smith Barney Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 76 sales totaling $929 million are on the schedule. A $139 million Cleveland City School District, Ohio, deal on Tuesday is the largest.
